entries.name: ms_tessellation.metallib
entries.role: GPU driver support shaders for Apple silicon / Apple GL-over-Metal
entries.note: Apple GPU driver internals (AGX family, GL shim); BifrOSt gets GPU drivers from Mesa/Vulkan (springboard/gpu) so there is no equivalent and no app depends on it

entries.name: MTLBVHBuilder.metallib
entries.role: Metal runtime helper shaders (blit, clear, resolve, indirect command support)
entries.note: Metal driver-internal helper kernel for Apple's own command encoding (blit, clear, resolve, acceleration-structure build, mesh-shader emulation). BifrOSt's GPU layer is Vulkan (springboard/gpu) and uses the Vulkan transfer, clear and resolve commands directly, so this shader has no counterpart to build.

entries.name: mlx.metallib
entries.role: 3D scene / RealityKit / USD rendering and geometry processing shaders
entries.note: The core array operations of a tensor compute library now exist on the CPU (kernel_array_ops.rs) with GLSL twins for matmul and softmax; neural-network layers are in bifrost-ui cnn_layers.rs. Quantised, FFT, convolution and sort kernels are not reproduced.
entries.ready_note: Ready (core operations): array kernels in springboard/render/src/kernel_array_ops.rs (matmul, transpose, unary maps exp/log/tanh/sigmoid/SiLU/GELU/ReLU, row bias, sum/mean/max/argmax along an axis, stable softmax and log-softmax, layer norm, RMS norm, cumulative sum, row gather, top-k), tests kernel_array_ops::tests; GLSL twins matmul.comp (existing) and the new array_softmax.comp (not wired to a pipeline). The large kernel catalogue of the reference library (quantised matmul, convolutions, FFT, sort) is not reproduced. Clean-room: written from public algorithm descriptions for the job this library serves; the metallib was not disassembled or compared.

entries.name: mvf.metallib
entries.role: 3D scene / RealityKit / USD rendering and geometry processing shaders
entries.note: Materials, lights and mesh layout exist as models, but no GPU rasteriser or physically based shader draws them yet.
entries.ready_note: Ready: the PBR material shading function in springboard/render/src/pbr.rs (GGX, Smith, Schlick Fresnel, metallic/roughness), tests pbr::tests. The per-point piece only; no GPU rasteriser or GLSL shader was added.

entries.name: mxi-binaryarchive.metallib
entries.role: 3D scene / RealityKit / USD rendering and geometry processing shaders
entries.note: A binary shader archive of the reference renderer; BifrOSt has no archive format for it.

entries.name: mxi.metallib
entries.role: 3D scene / RealityKit / USD rendering and geometry processing shaders
entries.note: A material-graph node subset and a scalar graph-to-GLSL compiler now exist in kernel_materialx.rs on top of shading_graph.rs and pbr.rs. The full node library (vector and colour graphs, standard surface, image nodes) is not implemented.
entries.ready_note: Ready (node subset and compiler): material-graph node library and graph compiler in springboard/render/src/kernel_materialx.rs (gradient and fractal noise, cellular noise, ramps, split, checkerboard, remap, contrast, HSV conversion, 2-D placement, normal-map node; ShaderGraph with CPU evaluation and GLSL code generation including a noise prelude that matches the CPU hash), tests kernel_materialx::tests. The simpler evaluator is shading_graph.rs; surface shading is pbr.rs. Only a subset of the standard node library is implemented, with scalar graphs; no GLSL shader file was added because the compiler emits GLSL at run time. Clean-room: written from public algorithm descriptions for the job this library serves; the metallib was not disassembled or compared.

entries.name: opticalFlowMetalLib.metallib
entries.role: Video frame rate conversion and optical flow
entries.note: BifrOSt has a CPU frame interpolator with a motion field and block motion estimation; no dense optical flow or GPU path. role inferred from the owning framework path; the metallib was not disassembled
entries.ready_note: Shader pass: block matcher (SAD full search) for frame-rate conversion; dense optical flow is not built, so the row covers the block-matching piece only.
